why: The statement asks only whether the series converges, so only a claim of unconditional convergence is 'whole'. Bounds on mu(pi) (Zeilberger-Zudilin, Bai) do not reach 5/2 and move no quantity the statement names, and threshold or criterion results (Alekseyev, Agama, Meiburg, Lopez Zapata) are reductions to unproven conditions, so all are 'none'. Garab's weighted series and Dan's generalised family are variants; Humphreys' partial sums are instances. Carella is set aside as not credible (several F10 signals together), and Mantzakouras-Lopez Zapata is knocked down by the co-author's withdrawal. The OpenAI claim is 'whole' and unreviewed. I called it doubtful, not not_credible: it is a week old, the convergence route (dyadic spacing from Theorem 1.1) is laid out explicitly, and no specific error has been found, but the jump to mu(pi)=2 is extraordinary. Its role is generated, because the README says an internal model produced the manuscripts and no human author is named. For Bai I chose 'assisted' over 'none' because 'proof development' is mathematics, even though the quote does not split it between the two models. That event is scope 'none' anyway.
doubts: openai-2026-10 and openai-math-017 are the same event (same manuscript and release date), split across two research stages, and I gave both identical answers. The README quote is about the whole repository ('vast majority'), not family 017 specifically. Humphreys' 'human-AI collaboration' does not say what Claude produced, so I answered none. Its scope is instances, so it is discarded either way.
